source_pages: CESAR - 2 Kitchen System.pdf printed p.314 / PDF 316, the H.96 block read whole 2026-08-26
extraction_note: DEMAND-DRIVEN, and narrow on purpose. The Avenida Primavera west wall holds three PF0631 - plain-door wall units, 600 x 960 x 350 - and Andriy asked for glass doors there on 2026-08-26. Only the H. 96 block of printed p.314 was taken. NOT extracted and not to be assumed: Glass wall units H. 60 (TD), H. 72 (TE), H. 84 (TG, the other half of the same printed page) and H. 120 (TJ), the glass tall units H. 138/198/210/222, and the tall-unit top elements with glass doors H. 36 and H. 48. The whole chapter is 'Glass display cabinet elements', printed p.305-315.
letter_note: TD = H.60, TE = H.72, TF = H.96, TG = H.84, TJ = H.120. THE F/G PAIR RUNS BACKWARDS AGAINST HEIGHT, exactly as it does in the plain wall chapter, where wall_h96.json already records 'F is H.96 and G is H.84: the letters run BACKWARDS across that pair, which is why they are a lookup and never a sequence.' That was read off printed p.245-247 and p.434; this is the same rule holding in a different chapter, read independently. A letter is a lookup.
collection_note: EVERY POSITION ON THIS PAGE CARRIES THE MARK 'N_Elle'. This project's header is MAXIMA 2.2 (estimate 2026/30829). The page does not say whether N_Elle is a COLLECTION restriction or the name of the framed-glass DOOR PROFILE - the book also has a whole chapter of 'N_Elle base units with framed door' (printed p.397+), which suggests the second, and suggesting is not knowing. ELDA QUESTION, and it decides whether this section applies to this kitchen at all.
carcass_note: The chapter's finishes page (printed p.306) prints its own carcass finish list and price bands 1-5, and repeats on every band: THE SIDE PANELS OF A GLASS DISPLAY CARCASS CANNOT BE CUSTOMISED - if an end panel in a customised finish is wanted on an end unit, a 22 mm side panel in that finish must be added ONTO the glass display unit. Not an issue in this kitchen (Andriy, 2026-08-26: the run ends against a filler, not an exposed end), recorded because it will be somewhere else.
door_options_note: Each position prints surcharges for the door treatment and the shelves rather than separate articles: '60 cm wide glass door with fabric 95', '60 cm wide ribbed glass door 95', 'Bronze glass shelves D.35 15', 'Fume glass shelves D.35 15' (H.96, one-door position). THE STANDARD DOOR IS THE POSITION ITSELF and carries none of these - Andriy, 2026-08-26: standard glass doors. The numbers are points, and no article code is printed beside any of them, which is the same shape as the wine cooler's stainless protection (Elda W3).

data.mounting_note: A glass wall unit hangs like any other wall unit; how high is a project decision the catalog does not state.
page_observations: The position drawings print 96 beside the carcass and 98,2 beside it - the same +2,2 cm appears at every height in this chapter (60/62,2, 72/74,2, 84/86,2, 96/98,2, 120/122,2). What the second number measures is NOT stated on the page and is deliberately not guessed here.
d. 35 is the only depth printed for glass wall units at any height.

PRINTED ON EVERY POSITION: 'Cannot be reduced in width, height or depth.' The p.548 modifications list already excludes 'tall or wall units with framed glass doors' from WIDTH reduction; this page states the same prohibition on the position itself AND extends it to HEIGHT and DEPTH.

glass_wall_door.description: Wall unit with glass door - 1 rh or lh glass door - 1 glass shelf or 2 glass shelves per height
glass_wall_door.notes: Two widths at H.96. ONE CODE, BOTH HANDS, like its plain-door cousin PF0631. CANNOT BE REDUCED IN WIDTH, HEIGHT OR DEPTH - printed on the position. Registry.WIDTH_MOD_FORBIDDEN already refuses a width change for anything whose description says 'glass'; the height half of the same printed sentence was wired on 2026-08-26 and cites THIS page rather than borrowing the width list.

front_layout.note: One glass door covering the full front, hinged on a vertical edge, hinge_side per order. THE FRAME IS 25 mm AND IT IS UCON'S NUMBER, NOT CESAR'S (Andriy, 2026-08-26). The catalog prints no frame section for a glass door on any page either of us could find: not the glass chapter (printed p.305-315), not 'Unit structure' (printed p.260, p.282-283, whose 'aluminium frame' is the structural frame of an open shelving unit and a different thing), not the technical pages (printed p.10-11), not the filler table (printed p.434). Andriy checked by eye as well and set 25, to be drawn CAD-style. So the object carries GLASS_FRAME_LABEL '(frame: DECLARED)' - deliberately not the aperture's '(cutout: INDICATIVE)', because an aperture's rails come from a machine's published specification and this comes from us. The pane is opaque and flat at full front thickness, which is the convention this engine chose for glass on 2026-08-22: a transparent material would show the room through a cabinet in every rendered view. NOTHING HERE IS A MANUFACTURING STATEMENT - the sheet is a drawing, not a production spec.

glass_wall_two_doors.description: Wall unit with glass doors - 2 glass doors - 2 glass shelves
glass_wall_two_doors.notes: One width at H.96. CANNOT BE REDUCED IN WIDTH, HEIGHT OR DEPTH - printed on the position.
